## Skills Service Manager

The Skills Service Manager (SSM) implements skill switching (life cycle events), global listen, splash screens, and notifications services. These are all implemented in Javascript and appear in the service registry alongside C/C++ based services on the robot. The SSM is launched when running skills locally, remotely, and on robot.

**These instructions are ONLY for running the SSM on a robot OR for folks CONTRIBUTING to the skills service manager. If you just want to USE the SSM and/or run skills in the simulator, see instructions [here](https://confluence.jibo.com/display/SKIL/How+to+Add+Skills+to+Be+and+Run+the+SSM).**

## Update latest SSM on your robot
1. Get the latest SSM on your computer
  2. If you are using github, then run this from your skill-service-manager location:

    ```
     git checkout master
     rm -rf node_modules
     rm -rf lib   
     npm install
     gulp debug
     ```
  2. If you are NOT using github, then run this on your computer:
  
    ```
     (First Time Only) create new directory on your computer where you will npm install SSM, like ~/npm
     cd into your npm directory (~/npm or whatever)
     rm -rf node_modules/skills-service-manager
     npm install skills-service-manager
     ```
2. Sync latest SSM on your robot
     ```
     cd into your updated skills-service-manager directory on robot
     run bin/run-on-robot.sh (uses your jibo-cli's default robot IP)          
     ```  
 
   

## Setup

1.  Clone the Skills Service Manager

         git clone git@github.jibo.com:sdk/skills-service-manager.git
         cd skills-service-manager
         git checkout dev
         
2.  Robot Setup (Required if you are going to run things on the robot)
   1. run `jibo build-version` to see which version your robot is on. Only >=v1.1.10 is supported for SSM.
   1. To add your SSH key to the robot, from the `ssm` root run: `./bin/utils/add-ssh-key.sh`
1.  You need to customize one file to your environment for testing simulated builds (**unfortunately this file is currently checked in. So change it, but try not to commit it unless you are making changes to other settings**). In `skills-service-manager/configs/remote.json`, set the skillsBaseDir to where the skill(s) you want to test with the skills-service-manager live. Ex. `"skillsBaseDir": "/Users/francoislaberge/jibo/skills",`
1. Getting your code npm linked, checking out the correct branches, and building it all:
  1. From `jibo`'s root run: (If you don't have `jibo` cloned, [the repo is here](https://github.jibo.com/sdk/jibo))

    ```
     git checkout dev
     npm install
     gulp watch
     ```
  1. From `skills-service-manager`'s root, run: (If you don't have `skills-service-manager` cloned, [the repo is here](https://github.jibo.com/sdk/skills-service-manager))

     ```
     git checkout dev
     npm link jibo
     npm install
     gulp watch
     ```
  1. From `jibo`'s root, run: `npm link skills-service-manager`
  1. From `jibo-cli`'s root, run: (If you don't have `jibo-cli` cloned, [the repo is here](https://github.jibo.com/sdk/jibo-cli))

     ```
     git checkout dev
     npm link skills-service-manager
     npm install
     gulp watch
     ```
   1. (Optional): To use Atom to launch skills do the following, from `jibo-sdk`'s root, run:

            ```
            git checkout master
            npm link jibo-cli
            npm link jibo
            npm install
            apm link .
            gulp watch
            ```
   1. For any skill you want to test with the skills service manager, you must run `npm link jibo` from its root.


## Running the Skills Service Manager

### On Robot

**IMPORTANT:** In order to test skill switching you need to `npm run sync` each skill to the robot before running the skill service manager.

**Run from the `skills-service-manager` root:**

  1. Run the skills service manager on the robot. (This syncs any changes made to the ssm, and kills any running dev-shell, ssm, or skill processes)
 
   ```bash
   ./bin/run-on-robot.sh
   ```
  2. The Dev Shell is now running (it's a part of the SSM now), so now run a skill by running the following from that skill's root folder: `jibo run --nosync` or `jibo debug --nosync` (if you want to debug your skill)

**To Debug the SSM, run the following:**

```bash
./bin/debug-skills-service-manager-on-robot.sh
```

### Gotchas
1. If you are adding a new directory to skills-service-manager that needs to be on the robot, make sure to add the specific directory to the buildroot makefile for jibo-ssm and follow directions to package up this change for the next build (see avida if you need assistance): `https://git.jibo.com/projects/PLAT/repos/buildroot.jibo/browse/package/jibo-ssm/jibo-ssm.mk`


### Packing for buildroot
1. Get your local skills-service-manager repo built and versioned properly
  1. run `gulp publish` (and `git push`) to get everything built 
  1. Update the release notes for that tag you pushed
2. Create tar and upload it to repository
  1. from skills-service-manager directory, run 
  
  ```bin/run/package.sh <version> <ldap user for repository.jibo.com> ```
  
  This will create a `../jibo-ssm-<version>.tar.gz`, upload it to http://repository.jibo.com/sdk/jibo-ssm/ and save off a shasum for the tar (`../jibo-ssm-sha`).
3. Make a branch of buildroot with your update
  1. Get latest buildroot.jibo#master (`https://git.jibo.com/projects/PLAT/repos/buildroot.jibo`)
    1. FIRST TIME: `git clone ssh://git@git.jibo.com:7999/plat/buildroot.jibo.git`
    1. OTHER TIMES: cd into buildroot.jibo, `git checkout master` and `git pull`
  1. Create a branch for your changes. 
    1. `git checkout -b <branch name>`: the branch name should follow convetion: `feature/<your name>/<short-description>` or `bugfix/<your name>/<short-description>` (e.g. `feature/avida/jibo-ssm-1.0.0-alpha.6`)
  1. Update your package's details (in `buildroot.jibo/package/jibo-ssm`)
    1. update the `jibo-ssm.hash` file to use the new shasum you created earlier (jibo-ssm-sha)
    1. update the `jibo-ssm.mk` file to specify the new version (used in the tar name)
    1. commit your changes and make note of the git commit # for next step
4. Notify Blair of your changes (in specific JIRA ticket for upcoming build)
  1. Follow directions in JIRA ticket on how to enter in your changes
  ```
  {color:red}
  repo: buildroot.jibo
  branch: <your branch name>
  commit: <your commit(s)>
  modifies: jibo-ssm, etc.
  
  <JIRA ticket that addresses this feature/bugfix>
  {color}
  ```
  ### Testing
  1. To run unit tests for SSM, run
  ```
  gulp test
  ```
  2. To run unit tests using Floss, run
  ```
  gulp unit-tests --debug
  ```
